To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the steel industry managers chose the strategies they did because they had a particular interpretation of their role and the role of the industry, which was based on their own history and the history of the industry, as well as the history of the union.

the steel industry was transformed from 1945 to the 1980s by the decisions of managers and union officials who had developed their own interpretations of their roles in the industry, and the roles of others.
the steel industry was transformed by a series of events, which were the result of a number of decisions by the major actors in the industry.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of organizational and industry history as an influence on managers′ interpretations of their world, and the possibilities and limitations of action within that interpretation.
how the steel industry came to be in its current state, and with the role of managers and their interpretations in this process.
the development of an understanding of how the steel industry came to its present condition, and how it may develop in the future.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the steel industry in the United States, in the period from 1945 to the mid‐1980s, was not in decline.
the steel industry has been a victim of the actions of the managers and union leaders who have worked in it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the steel industry is a complex system of interdependent actors.
the industry was not transformed by external forces.
managers in the steel industry, in their attempts to deal with their environment, chose to act in ways that were based on a set of beliefs about their industry.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the history of the industry and the organizations within it, and how managers understand that history and the industry, is a significant influence on how managers choose to act.
organizational and industry history are important in shaping the way managers interpret their world.
the steel industry is an industry which is not only about steel production and sales, but about the production of steel industry narratives.
